page: Amazon Web Services c8gd.2xlarge is an ARM-based compute-optimized virtual instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by the AWS Graviton processor family utilizing the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture. The instance provides 8 dedicated physical cores corresponding to 8 vCPUs clocked at 2.8 GHz, with a single hardware thread per core. Memory provision consists of 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:2 compute-optimized ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance also integrates a direct-attached 474 GB NVMe SSD local storage volume and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Synthetic benchmark testing indicates steady middle-tier performance across integer and floating-point computations. The instance registered a Geekbench single-core score of 1760.0 and a multi-core score of 9615.0, complemented by a multi-core stress-ng metric of 13638.03. Memory bandwidth reaches 162.67 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 924.65 GB/sec for small cached blocks. In data workloads, the system sustained 16.71 million Redis SET operations per second and 19.42 GB/sec of static web serving throughput. PassMark CPU encryption registered in the bottom 25th percentile at 1512.16, and larger AI prompt evaluations demonstrated reduced throughput, reflecting architecture and hardware cache limits for heavy generative AI workloads.

With dedicated cores and integrated high-speed local NVMe storage, the c8gd.2xlarge delivers predictable execution without resource contention from simultaneous multithreading. The 1:2 memory configuration keeps per-core infrastructure costs economical for CPU-bound tasks. This instance profile is well aligned with continuous integration pipelines, software compilation, batch processing, static web serving, and distributed caching environments requiring high I/O throughput on temporary scratch storage.
